# dsp::envelope

Module file: `modules/dsp/envelope.mla`

`Adsr` is an allocation-free attack/decay/sustain/release gain envelope for
realtime audio, used as the amp envelope of the Mla Drum sampler.

```rust
mod dsp::envelope;
use dsp::envelope::Adsr;

var env: Adsr = Adsr::new(48000.0f);
env.set_attack_seconds(0.005f);
env.set_decay_seconds(0.3f);
env.set_sustain(0.6f);
env.set_release_seconds(0.2f);
env.gate_on();                    // note-on
let gain: f32 = env.process();    // once per sample
env.gate_off();                   // note-off
if !env.is_active() { /* voice finished */ }
```

The attack is a linear ramp to full scale. Decay and release are exponential,
and their times are measured to a 60 dB fall. The envelope goes idle once it
drops below -80 dB.

- `gate_on()` restarts the attack from the current level, so retriggers do not
  click.
- A sustain of `0` ends the envelope after the decay. That suits one-shot drums
  that ignore note-off.
- `gate_off()` on an idle envelope does nothing. `reset()` silences it
  immediately.

Attack is clamped to `0..10 s`, decay and release to `0..30 s` (0 = instant),
and sustain to `0..1`. `current_stage()` reports 0 idle, 1 attack, 2 decay,
3 sustain or 4 release. `set_sample_rate()` keeps the stage times in seconds.
